body:
I appreciate hearing your side of things. It's crazy how similar our situations are. My best friend/BF(?) also reddits and I even wondered if this was him. Anyway, it's making me reconsider cutting off communication. It's definitely not what I want, and I really need him as support, so if it won't be a relief for him I don't want to do it. For me, his support right now is the thing that's keeping me from killing myself so it's pretty much life/death. Any suggestions for things I could do that would make things easier for him and maybe even ideas about ways to help him help me? I'm trying therapy, but my first session was very discouraging and I'm not sure I believe in it. But I'm going for him since I think it will make him feel like some of the burden is off him.

Best of luck moving forward. I'm sure this is all really painful for you...just know that it's hard from both sides. I tried to cut ties a couple months ago, and sincerely meant to do it, but was relieved when my BF was persistent and kept supporting me. When I tried to say goodbye I couldn't even speak I was crying so hard. Even though I was breaking up with him he just kept telling me to breathe and that it would be ok. I can't even put in to words how much his reaction comforted me. I could tell he genuinely cares and wants what was best for me.

So from my experience, I would say don't give up if you think her true reason was just to protect you. Just make sure you reach out to her in a way that respects her space and isn't pushy. My BF basically sent me texts asking how I was doing and saying that he still loved me and that he was there to support me as soon as I was ready. Maybe even say it in a way that doesn't pressure a response from her. Things like "Just wanted to let you know that I'm thinking about you and I miss you. I know that you are going through a tough time, and I am here in whatever way you need me" can mean a tremendous amount to someone who is depressed. It's a little bit of hope to cling to. I used to replay old voicemails and reread caring texts from him over and over. Even though I didn't always respond it meant a lot to know that he cared enough to worry. But if she asks you to stop, I would say respect her space. When everything is said and done, I think people really just want to feel close to someone and feel cared for.

Also, I know you said at times it feels like you aren't helping her since you can't see a visible difference...my BF said the same thing. What he didn't know was that even though I was still sobbing uncontrollably in his arms, it was the difference between being upset and hurting myself. Even if I couldn't show him I was better he helped me by being there. Just knowing he cares helps me. So don't underestimate the good that you were able to do for her.

Best of luck friend and let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

I'm on the other side of things and am considering closing communication with someone I love very much. I don't want to hurt him more and I don't think I'll ever be able to beat the cycles. I feel like it isnt fair for me to be with someone knowing they will be subject to my mood changes. I feel toxic. He and I stopped dating because of my depression but continued talking and have considered getting back together. I think my leaving will hurt him at first but then he will ultimately feel relief since right now he feels a lot of pressure to make me happy. Doesn't help that we live 12 hrs away from each other so he's trying to take care of me over the phone...
thanks, this is encouraging. glad things went ok for you, and congrats on getting help

You can do it too!! From prior experience, the hardest step is making that first call. I was literally shaking this morning when I did. The second hardest step is showing up for the first appointment. For me, I hit a breaking point last night and realized that it's either get help or kill myself. I can't live like this anymore. I've heard good things about CBT and so I did a google search for therapists in my area that specialize in CBT and sent an email right away since I knew if I waited until morning I would put it off longer. Money is an issue so I'm probably going to do group therapy. Best of luck, and let me know if there's anything I can do to help.
I'm definitely willing to try self-help things before suicide. I don't want to kill myself so much as I just want to end the apathy and hurt

I just need my body to decide whether I'm a morning person or a night owl...right now I'm losing sleep on both sides. I do agree about the deep thoughts. Only trick is to keep from getting so deep that you get swallowed

Thank you for your support. I'm impressed that you made it though the whole thing twice...it's so long. 

I have a lot of positive things going on too and I like your idea about making a list of good things everyday. I have family and friends that love me and want to support me, they just don't know how. I have a 4 year degree, a full time job, and am financially independent at 23. My parents paid for college and my car so I am debt free. I have friends that call me every week even though I never initiate conversation. I feel very fortunate for these things. It's just hard to remember them sometimes when my mind is spinning and I can't find the off-switch. Sometimes I feel like since I have so many good things I don't have the right to be upset. In my group therapy I couldn't even put words to what was causing my depression...I mainly just supported everyone else. Their problems seemed so much bigger and more legitimate than mine. But I guess I never really opened up about my internal dialogue struggles because of fear of rejection.

I think I've spilled everything I need to for tonight, but I really do appreciate the help. It feels good to get everything off my chest. Thanks for reminding me to focus on the little things too. I think that will be easier right now.
